input.message: Make this little bird page pretty and easy to read on a phone. Make its main heading blue. Keep the button working and keep everything in index.html with no downloads.

result.answer:
I updated `index.html` in place. It now has a mobile viewport, a readable card layout, responsive heading size, comfortable line spacing, a full-width touch-friendly button, and the main `<h1>` heading styled with `color: blue`. The button remains wired to the same fact behavior through inline JavaScript in the same file, with no external scripts, styles, fonts, images, or downloads.

I ran the named check `bird_page_requirements`. It exited with status 0, stdout was `ok`, and stderr was empty. The check verified the viewport, blue heading rule, mobile-friendly layout properties, button/fact IDs, click handler wiring, and absence of external resource patterns. This is a static check, so it verifies the page contents and wiring but does not render the page in a real browser.
